summary:
This record covers Sud, a region of Italy, and stands under the national framework of the Italian Republic. No region-specific statute, court ruling or administrative measure addressing gender identity or sexual orientation was identified for Sud, so the regional assessment rests on documented incidents and on custody practice.

ILGA-Europe's annual country review for Italy, published in February 2025, finds a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence against LGBTI people during 2024, with incidents reported almost monthly. Among the incidents it records is a scooter-mounted assault in March 2025 on a young man in Scampia, a district of Naples.

On 13 October 2025 a 63-year-old man was arrested in Torre Annunziata, in the province of Naples, after making stabbing threats against a young LGBTQIA+ activist. Il Gazzettino described the case as a grave homophobic episode in the Naples area.
tangentialFactors:
Both documented incidents fall in the Campania part of the region, in and around Naples and its province. The sources record nothing for Puglia, Basilicata, Calabria or Molise, and that silence reflects the coverage of the monitors rather than a finding that those areas are free of anti-LGBT violence.

The violence recorded is street-level and directed at identified individuals: an assault from a moving scooter and stabbing threats against an activist. Neither incident involved state agents, and no region-specific police, municipal or school measure addressing anti-LGBT violence in Sud appears in the inventory.

ILGA-Europe's review is national in scope and does not break its figures down by region, so Sud cannot be ranked against other Italian regions on the strength of these sources. The counts behind the review's finding of rising violence are raw totals with no per-region denominator attached.
localsOnly:
Trans detainees held in Sud stand in the ordinary men's and women's prison circuit. No region-specific unit or facility for transgender prisoners is documented for the region, and no separate custody rule for trans detainees appears in the inventory.

LGBTQIA+ activism in the Naples area carries documented personal risk for residents as well as visitors. A young activist was the target of stabbing threats in Torre Annunziata in October 2025, and a young man was assaulted in Scampia, Naples, in March 2025.
outOfScopeNotes:
ILGA-Europe's review is dated February 2025 yet records an incident dated March 2025; the dating is unresolved in the source and is reproduced here as given.

Whether either documented incident was prosecuted, and whether any charge was brought as a hate crime or on a bias motive, is not sourced. The inventory records an arrest in Torre Annunziata but no outcome.

No dedicated transgender detention facility exists in Sud. The only Italian special-unit initiative of that kind was announced in 2010 for Pozzale, a prison in Tuscany, and had not opened as of 2013 reporting; whether any comparable unit has since been created anywhere in Italy is unresolved here, and no region-specific custody provision for Sud was identified.

The inventory contains no region-specific data on legal gender recognition, identity documents, entry screening, facilities access or health care for Sud; those questions stand at the national layer of the Italian Republic and are not evidenced at regional level.
